title: The 2026 Berggruen Prize Essay Competition Topic: ‘A New Axial Age?’ | NOEMA
gist: Noema's editor-in-chief frames the 2026 Berggruen Prize essay topic around Karl Jaspers' Axial Age, arguing that genetic engineering, synthetic biology and AI are reviving foundational religious and ethical questions at a moment of no shared ideational framework and dwindling trust in inherited faiths and institutions. The piece is largely a $50,000 competition announcement, and its most concrete signal is the prize's strict AI-usage rule: generative AI may not create content or substitute original thought, and all use must be disclosed on the front page or the entry is disqualified.

themes.theme: Axial Age as a framework for the present

insights.claim: Karl Jaspers' Axial Age describes the period over two millennia ago when the great religions, philosophical outlooks and ethical systems were born nearly simultaneously — China's Confucianism, India's Upanishads and Buddhism, Homer's Greece and the Hebrew prophets — a 'hinge of history' where events at one point disproportionately shape the future trajectory.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: A hinge-of-history frame is how elite intellectual institutions are now positioning the AI era, which shapes the philanthropic and policy agendas that follow.
insights.locator: Karl Jaspers, the German Swiss philosopher

insights.claim: The competition topic follows an essay by Otto Scharmer arguing we may be entering a second Axial Age and a conversation with complexity scientist Stuart Kauffman titled 'Emergence Is Not Engineering'.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: Signals which intellectual lineage — complexity and emergence rather than engineering control — is gaining traction among the institutions funding big-picture technology thought.
insights.locator: It follows an essay in Noema by Otto Scharmer

themes.theme: Technology forcing a return to first principles

insights.claim: Recent leaps in genetic engineering, synthetic biology and artificial intelligence are resurrecting the religious and ethical imagination by stirring foundational questions about human origins and destiny, while the planetary climate crisis puts even species survival at risk.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: Biotech and AI are being framed as metaphysical rather than merely economic disruptions, which predicts values-based rather than cost-based political resistance.
insights.locator: Recent leaps in science and technology

insights.claim: With no shared ideational framework and dwindling trust in bequeathed faiths and institutions, humanity is being forced back to first principles and the time for a synchronous global rethink appears to have arrived.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: Institutional trust collapse plus technological upheaval is the stated precondition for ideological realignment — the environment in which new governance coalitions form.
insights.quote: With no shared ideational framework and dwindling trust in bequeathed faiths and institutions, humanity is being forced back to first principles.

insights.claim: The Berggruen Prize Essay Competition awards $50,000 for essays submitted in English and Chinese, with winning essays published to give readers insight into both Eastern and Western perspectives, and for 2026 it is accepting creative fiction.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: An explicitly bilingual East-West intellectual platform funded at scale is a soft-power channel worth tracking alongside formal diplomacy.
insights.locator: The competition awards a prize of $50,000

insights.claim: The competition bars entrants from using generative AI to create content or substitute original thought and requires engagement with primary sources rather than AI-generated summaries, permitting AI only for proofreading, as excerpted supporting material when AI itself is the research subject, or for translation — with all usage disclosed on the front page on pain of disqualification.
insights.speaker: Nathan Gardels
insights.so_what: An early concrete template for institutional AI-authorship rules — mandatory disclosure with narrow permitted uses is the norm likely to propagate through academia, publishing and grantmaking.
insights.quote: Entrants must not use generative AI to create content or substitute original thought.
